## Errors

Errors always use the canonical body
`{ code, message, details? }`. The `code`\nis stable and machine-readable; `message` is human-readable and may change;\n`details`

is an optional, unstructured bag.

| Code | HTTP | Meaning |
| - | - | - |
| `UNAUTHORIZED` | 401 | Missing, invalid, revoked,
or orphaned key |\n| `OAUTH_REQUIRED` | 401 | The **target MCP server** needs an OAuth grant; distinct from a bad key |\n| `AUTH_
REQUIRED` | 403 | The **target MCP server** allowed the connection and asked for sign-in on this call. `details.authChallenge` car
ries the parsed challenge. Your key is fine; see [Sign-in challenges](#sign-in-challenges) |\n| `FORBIDDEN` | 403 | Key is valid b
ut not allowed to do this, or the **target MCP server** rejected the credentials MCPJam presented (retrying with a different MCPJa
m key will not help; reconnect or re-authorize the server) |\n| `VALIDATION_ERROR` | 400 | Malformed body or parameters |\n| `NOT_
FOUND` | 404 | Unknown project, server, or resource |\n| `CONFLICT` | 409 | The resource isn't in a state that accepts this write,
such as a stale `expectedRevision`, a duplicate name, or an environment that can't currently be launched. Re-read and retry |\n|
`FEATURE_NOT_SUPPORTED` | 422 | The target server doesn't support this MCP capability |\n| `RATE_LIMITED` | 429 | Too many request
s; see [Rate limits](#rate-limits) |\n| `SERVER_UNREACHABLE` | 502 | Could not connect to the target MCP server |\n| `TIMEOUT` | 5

04 | The target MCP server connected but didn't respond in time |
| `INTERNAL_ERROR` | 500 | Something failed on our side |

Ne
w error codes may be **added** over time; treat unknown codes as\nnon-retryable failures unless the HTTP status says otherwise.\n\

n### Sign-in challenges

Some MCP servers allow the connection and ask for sign-in only on a protected
call. The API never star

ts a sign-in. It reports the challenge instead:

* **HTTP 401 from the MCP server** on `tools/call`: the API answers
 `403 AUT
H_REQUIRED`. `details.authChallenge` carries the parsed challenge:\n its `source` (`http_401`), and the `error`, `requiredScope`,
and\n `resourceMetadataUrl` the server sent, when present.\n* **An `isError` result carrying `_meta[\"mcp/www_authenticate\"]`**
(the\n ChatGPT convention): the call succeeds, and the `CallToolResult` is returned\n unchanged with an additive `authChallenge

` field (`source:
 "tool_result_meta"`). A field the server already set under that name is never
 overwritten.

`AUTH_REQU
IRED` is not `UNAUTHORIZED`: your MCPJam key is fine, so a different\nkey will not help. Complete the OAuth flow for that server y
ourself, upload the\ntoken to one of its [accounts](#server-accounts), and call again. See\n[Mid-session sign-in](https://docs.mcp

jam.com/inspector/lazy-authentication.md).

## Rate limits

Each key gets **60 requests per minute** sustained, with bursts up

to **10**.
Exceeding it returns `429 RATE_LIMITED` with a `Retry-After` header (in
seconds):

```http theme={"theme":"css-

variables"}
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 7

{ "code": "RATE_LIMITED", "message": "API key rate limit ex

ceeded. Slow down and retry." }
```

Honor `Retry-After`, add jittered exponential backoff, and expect these limits
to be tun

ed during the preview.

Other `429`s, the per-minute brakes and daily budgets described with the
endpoints below, carry `Retry-
After` whenever the refusal knows when it\nlifts, which is the ordinary case. Treat it as a hint that is usually there\nrather tha
n a guarantee: a refusal that reaches you without one still needs\nyour backoff, so **never** block waiting for a header that may

not come.

## Endpoints

Each endpoint is fully documented (request and response schemas, examples,
and an interactive playgr

ound) under **Endpoints** in the sidebar.

**Catalog**: discover the IDs everything else takes:

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |\n| `GET /me` | The account behind the key |\n| `GET /organizations` | The organizations the caller belongs to, where `or
ganizationId` comes from. A key is bound to one organization and only ever sees that one |\n| `GET /projects` | Projects the key c
an access (optionally `?organizationId=`) |\n| `GET /projects/{projectId}/servers` | The project's saved MCP servers |\n| `GET /pr
ojects/{projectId}/servers/{serverId}/revisions` | A server's stored revisions, newest first: captures of its tools and server inf
o, recorded whenever they change (`?limit=&cursor=`) |\n| `GET /projects/{projectId}/servers/{serverId}/revisions/{revisionNumber}
` | One revision: every tool's definition and the server info it reported. Fields listed in `droppedFields` were too large to stor
e, so they are unknown, not absent |\n| `GET /projects/{projectId}/servers/{serverId}/revisions/{revisionNumber}/diff` | What chan
ged since the revision before, or since `?from=`: tools added, removed and changed, and server info changes with both values. A fi
eld listed in `droppedFields.from` or `droppedFields.to` was not stored on that side, so a change to it is unknown |\n| `GET /proj
ects/{projectId}/eval-suites` | The project's eval suites, with latest-run summaries |\n| `GET`, `POST /projects/{projectId}/clien
ts` | List clients, or create one from a template or full config |\n| `GET`, `PATCH`, `DELETE /projects/{projectId}/clients/{clien
t}` | Read, edit, or delete a client. The path segment takes a client **name or ID** |\n| `POST /projects/{projectId}/clients/{cli
ent}/servers` | Replace the client's server attachments (a replacement; omitted servers are detached) |\n| `POST /projects/{projec
tId}/clients/{client}/duplicate` | Copy a client's current config into a new client |\n| `GET /chat-sessions` | Chat sessions (`?p

rojectId=&status=&limit=&before=`) |

**Project environments**: the named execution bundles (one host, optionally a
standalone
server group) that eval suites and goals run against. Reads need\nproject membership. Archiving needs project admin and is revisio

ned: pass the
`revision` you last read back as `expectedRevision`, and a stale value returns
`CONFLICT` (409).

| Endpoint | W
hat it does |\n| - | - |\n| `GET /projects/{projectId}/environments` | List environments (`?includeArchived=true` to include archi
ved ones) |\n| `GET /projects/{projectId}/environments/{environmentId}` | Read one environment |\n| `GET /projects/{projectId}/env
ironments/{environmentId}/resolve` | Preview the host config and closed server set this environment resolves to right now |\n| `PO
ST /projects/{projectId}/environments/{environmentId}/archive` | Archive it. The environment is kept, and its name is freed for a

new one |

**Server diagnostics & primitives** (`/projects/{projectId}/servers/{serverId}/...`):

| Endpoint | What it does |\
n| - | - |\n| `POST .../validate` | Connect, initialize, and capture a capability snapshot |\n| `POST .../doctor` | Full health wo
rkflow: probe → connect → initialize → capabilities |\n| `POST .../check-oauth` | Does this server require an OAuth grant? |\n| `P
OST .../tools` | List the server's tools |\n| `POST .../tools/call` | Execute a tool; returns the MCP `CallToolResult` plus additi
ve `durationMs`, and `authChallenge` when the result asks for sign-in (see [Sign-in challenges](#sign-in-challenges)) |\n| `POST .
../prompts` | List the server's prompts |\n| `POST .../prompts/get` | Render a prompt; returns the MCP `GetPromptResult` verbatim

|
| `POST .../resources` | List the server's resources |
| `POST .../resources/read` | Read one resource by URI |
| `POST .../e
xport` | One JSON snapshot of tools, resources, and prompts |\n| `GET`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE .../accounts[/{account}]` | The se
rver's accounts. See [Server accounts](#server-accounts) |\n| `POST .../oauth/import-tokens` | **Deprecated.** Uploads to your def
ault account; use `PUT .../accounts/{account}`. See [The deprecated import route](#the-deprecated-import-route) |\n\n**Eval runs**

(`/projects/{projectId}/...`):

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `POST .../eval-suites` | Author-only: create a suite
+ its test cases from `name` + `serverIds` + a default `model` + `tests`, WITHOUT running it; responds `201` + `suiteId`. Each tes
